content.comment_body: How can I fully disable password protection in [product_name]? The checkbox for disabling this feature is currently not selectable. I know the password and don't need to reset it; I'd just like to avoid password prompts entirely.
Are you connected online when setting the access properties?
Are you sure you're using [product_name] version [version_no]? It doesn't seem like it.
Yes, I'm sure. I'm using [product_name] [version_no] on Linux.

My question was about [product_name] [version_no], not [product_name] [version_no]. See the attached images. There are screenshots from two different versions showing the differences. For [product_name] [version_no] the password feature isn't active.
I don't see any screenshot, was the wrong file uploaded? I have [product_name] [article_no]. Not sure what you mean, but currently I can't avoid using the correct password in [product_name].
This feature isn't available in [product_name] [version_no], which is why the option is disabled.

Does [product_name] [version_no] mean new hardware or a firmware upgrade? Does this mean I can't skip entering a password every time with my current module? The terminology and numbering are confusing for me. Thanks for clarifying.
Sorry, the attachment was incorrect. Here's the correct one. Do you notice the menu structure differences?
[product_name] [version_no] is a completely new model. Check this product note from [company_name] about the release details for [product_name] [version_no].
The password is already stored on the hardware. To reset or disable it, use the Tools menu: Tools > Transfer > Clear User Program and Password.
If you haven't saved the original program, it's best to upload and save it as [product_name] or other file formats before clearing both the program and password.
I think there's a misunderstanding. Your suggestion doesn't apply here.
Your suggestion is also not relevant for this scenario.
Let the user try it first; it won't cause any harm.
Your comments suggest you still don't understand the root issue.
That doesn't solve the issue; I've already tested it.

It appears neither the original poster nor user M111 understand the actual issue. In [product_name] [version_no], no password is assigned to the 'LWE & [product_name] access' function since it's not present in that firmware. That's why the option is disabled and can't be unchecked. There's also a screenshot attached showing the access control for a [article_no] standard module, with the menu item disabled as well.
I tried entering a blank password, but that's not permitted. Using Tools > Transfer > Clear did resolve it for me.

I tried entering a blank password, but that's not allowed. Using Tools > Transfer > Clear worked for me. However, in this particular case, your suggestion does not address the original poster's issue. The problem is wanting to deactivate a password feature that's only relevant for [product_name] [version_no]. In previous versions, the password function isn't available, so you can't deactivate something that's inactive.

I tried entering a blank password, but that's not permitted. Using Tools > Transfer > Clear worked for me. Regarding the topic, your advice is not solving the original poster's issue; the password cannot be deactivated in earlier versions because it's not active. For [product_name] [version_no], it's not possible to manage this function. I use [product_name] [version_no] and can remove transfer passwords, but the checkbox remains disabled. Resetting erases the old password, and no field for the old password is available anymore. Let the user retry. The disabled checkbox shouldn't be considered the method for disabling the password. If you can't offer a solution, your advice is incorrect.
After disabling the password, the checkbox will still appear disabled. But during upload or download with [product_name], you no longer need to enter a password, provided removal was successful.

I'm aware it's impossible without resetting, meaning the password needs to be erased differently. The menu option won't work, entering a blank password or trying to uncheck the disabled box won't succeed.
Again, I don't think you understood the problem...

There's no solution for this. The 'LSC & LWE Access' option only works with [product_name] [version_no], not older modules, which is why it's disabled. The check box can't be removed for the same reason. See the attached screen recording showing the effect in [product_name] [version_no], both with and without a password.
I've successfully done this with [product_name] [version_no]; just clear the password offline and transfer it online. Otherwise, you'll still get prompted for a password during upload/download.

The real issue is that you don't understand what the problem is. For me, the discussion is closed. I don't want to waste time explaining further. I'm only sorry for other users who get confused by these exchanges.

The real issue is that you don't understand. I'll leave it here and won't explain anymore; it's been unproductive. It's easy for me, if anyone finds it frustrating just skip it. Use Tools > Transfer > Clear user program and password, or File > Property > Program password > Clear > OK, and then download to the module once. Let the user try and see if their issue is resolved. If they're using [product_name] [version_no], the checkbox can enable/disable the password.
You can definitely avoid it in [product_name] [version_no].
That doesn't help, I still receive a prompt for the access password in [product_name].

And the award goes to...? This time I made a careless mistake myself—I didn't notice the wrong port was selected in [product_name]. I have dual network cards, and programs would load regardless, but [product_name] auto-selected the incorrect port during installation. After choosing the proper network interface, the password prompt disappeared. Thank you to everyone who helped!
Congratulations! Have a great day!

The password prompt made you assume it was related to the menu item 'LSC & LWE Access.' That's why your question focused there, but that wasn't the actual issue. If the problem had been described as a password prompt when transferring a program, I could've highlighted the incorrect interface selection. This issue is quite well-known.

analysis.insight_summary: There is significant confusion among users regarding password protection in [product_name], particularly because the option to disable it is often grayed out. Many users are unclear about the distinctions between different hardware versions and firmware releases of [product_name], which leads to misunderstanding about feature availability. The inability to turn off password prompts disrupts usage and increases frustration, compounded by unclear terminology and inconsistent features between device revisions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to completely turn off password protection in [product_name] and eliminate password prompts during configuration and access. They also wish for clearer product terminology and more consistent feature availability across different [product_name] versions.
